_comment_interfaces: lan_if/wan_if are rewritten at every boot by pisowifi-detect while auto_detect_interfaces is true; set it false to pin them.
_comment_wan_management: true keeps SSH/portal/ping reachable on the UPLINK side. Bench bring-up only; seal.sh forces it false.
_comment_admin_lan_access: Who may open /admin. whitelist (default) = customers refused once any device is whitelisted; off = customer network never, uplink port yes; tailscale = ONLY over the Tailscale tunnel, no physical network at all; any = no restriction, the recovery setting. The customer portal is never gated by this. seal.sh resets it, because a Tailscale-only card cannot be set up before Tailscale is enrolled.
_comment_wan_ssh: true opens SSH (and ping) on the uplink port but NOT the portal -- for an owner who administers over Tailscale yet wants one trusted machine able to shell in over the wire. Key-only SSH is what actually restricts who gets in; the firewall cannot pin to a laptop whose DHCP address moves. seal.sh does not clear this, so decide before imaging.
_comment_wan_admin: true serves the ADMIN PAGE ONLY (no SSH) on the uplink port, and survives seal.sh. Required when admin_lan_access is off, otherwise sealing leaves admin unreachable.
_comment_default_speed: Per-customer cap applied to NEW sessions, by profile name from speed_profiles. Ships as 'default' (5 Mbit down / 3 up) rather than unlimited: one customer streaming 4K should not be able to take the whole uplink from everyone else. Existing sessions keep the speed they were created with.
_comment_anti_tether: anti_tether watches for a customer sharing their session over a phone hotspot, by recording which TTLs each MAC sends at; a MAC showing two at once is forwarding for something. It reports only. anti_tether_enforce additionally sends TTL=1 to CONFIRMED sharers, which reaches the phone but dies at anything behind it. Never blanket-drop on a low TTL: an on-device VPN decrements every packet a customer sends, and doing so cut real customers off the internet.
